source: Assumed synchronous rotation: a planet 3.2 stellar radii from its star is expected to be tidally locked, and no rotation period or obliquity of KELT-9b is measured (Gaudi et al. 2017, Mansfield et al. 2020 and Ahlers et al. 2020 assume it). Pole, prime meridian and rate are computed from the hosted orbit in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kelt-9b.json.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is the orbit normal (prograde spin); +X points at the host star at each instant, so longitude 0 is the substellar point; east longitude, the direction of rotation.
qualification: Tidal locking and a spin axis on the orbit normal are assumptions, not measurements: neither the rotation period nor the obliquity of KELT-9b is measured.
